title: Glucobuddy: Detecting Diabetes Risk Using Machine Learning
summary: The v1 preprint evaluates supervised models for classifying the PIMA dataset diabetes label from health indicators; a held-out 80/20 evaluation reports performance. This qualifies only as a narrow retrospective dataset classification result, not future-risk prediction, clinical screening, or patient benefit.
ai_technology: Methods train supervised Logistic Regression, KNN, Gaussian Naive Bayes, Random Forest and SVM models using the dataset outcome label and health features; abstract and Methods differ on algorithm count, so the Results section’s five-model table was followed.
organization: Affiliation not stated in the indexed abstract reviewed

evidence.tested: Held-out table reports Random Forest accuracy 81.0% and ROC-AUC 85.4%; the text elsewhere selects Logistic Regression/Naive Bayes, so no single best-model claim is made.
evidence.unknown: PIMA dataset has 768 records, 80/20 stratified split and five-fold training cross-validation. The source notes the narrow demographic dataset, no real-world patient testing and no clinical validation; outcome is existing diabetes status, not prospective risk.
evidence.ai_role: Methods train supervised Logistic Regression, KNN, Gaussian Naive Bayes, Random Forest and SVM models using the dataset outcome label and health features; abstract and Methods differ on algorithm count, so the Results section’s five-model table was followed.
